# changelog-from-commits

> A command-line tool that generates a formatted CHANGELOG.md from git commit
> history following the Conventional Commits specification. Zero configuration,
> zero runtime dependencies. Requires Node.js 18 or newer. MIT licensed.

Install and run with `npx changelog-from-commits` in any git repository.

## What it does

Reads every commit since the last git tag, parses each subject against the
Conventional Commits grammar (`type(scope)!: description`), groups the results
into sections (Features, Bug Fixes, Performance Improvements, and so on), links
each entry to its pull request or commit, and prepends a new release section to
CHANGELOG.md above the newest existing release.

## Key behaviours

- Breaking changes come from a `!` after the type/scope or a `BREAKING CHANGE:`
  footer, and are rendered in a prominent section at the top of the release.
- The repository URL is detected from the `origin` remote. GitHub, GitLab and
  Bitbucket link shapes are built correctly; other hosts fall back to GitHub's.
- Non-conventional commits are skipped by default and the count is reported;
  `--include-all` collects them into an "Other Changes" section.
- Merge commits are always dropped.
- A commit and its revert inside the same range cancel out.
- Gitmoji prefixes (`✨ feat: ...`, `:sparkles: feat: ...`) are understood.
- Alternate type spellings (`feature`, `bugfix`, `doc`) fold onto canonical types.
- Prereleases: a stable release starts from the last *stable* tag, so commits
  that went into a beta are not lost.

## Common commands

- `npx changelog-from-commits` — everything since the last tag
- `npx changelog-from-commits --dry-run` — preview without writing
- `npx changelog-from-commits --version 1.4.0` — set the release heading
- `npx changelog-from-commits --all --force` — rebuild the whole file from every tag
- `npx changelog-from-commits --tag-prefix web-v --path packages/web` — one monorepo package

## Monorepos

`--tag-prefix` scopes the commit range to a package's tags; `--path` scopes which
commits are included. Both are usually needed together — with only the tag prefix,
a package's changelog lists every other package's commits since that tag.
